skill.name: react-doctor
skill.description: Diagnoses React projects for correctness, security, accessibility, performance, bundle size, and architecture issues, then guides scoped fixes, validation, and rule configuration.

content.value_statement: React projects accumulate correctness, accessibility, performance, and architecture issues. React Doctor runs targeted diagnostics and guides prioritized fixes with regression checks.
actual_capabilities: Runs React Doctor against changed files or the whole codebase.
Reports a 0-100 health score and detailed issue locations.
Supports changed-scope, line-scope, verbose, and score-only scans.
Prioritizes errors before warnings during cleanup.
Explains individual rules and available configuration controls.
Applies narrow rule, category, tag, and output-surface configuration changes.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npx, and access to the React Doctor package.
Uses react-doctor@latest, so behavior can change between runs.
Full triage depends on remote react.doctor prompts and network access.
Diagnostic results require human review before committing changes.

use_cases.title: Check a finished feature
use_cases.description: Scan changed React code, compare the health score, and fix regressions before committing.

use_cases.title: Triage an existing application
use_cases.description: Scan the full codebase, prioritize errors and warnings, apply fixes, and validate the result.

use_cases.title: Manage diagnostic rules
use_cases.description: Explain noisy rules and select narrow configuration controls for a shared React project.

prompt_templates.title: Check changed React code
prompt_templates.prompt: Run React Doctor on changed code. Summarize score changes, errors, warnings, and recommended fixes before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner regression check before a commit

prompt_templates.title: Clean the full codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the complete React project. Prioritize errors before warnings, fix the highest-impact findings, and rerun the same scan.

prompt_templates.title: Explain and configure a rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why [rule] fired. Recommend the narrowest configuration change, apply it only after approval, and validate the result.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a full triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full React Doctor triage. Filter findings, prioritize fixes, edit the working tree, rerun diagnostics, and report remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Explain why the array-index key rule fired.
output: Index keys can associate component state with the wrong item after list reordering.
Use a stable item identifier when available.
Disable the rule only when the list order and membership are guaranteed to remain fixed.

best_practices: Review commands and requested scope before allowing package execution or file edits.
Fix errors before warnings, then rerun the same scope to measure regression.
Use the narrowest rule configuration and validate behavior after every change.
anti_patterns: Do not run mutable latest packages or remote playbooks without trusted network access.
Do not disable a rule before understanding why it fired and confirming user intent.
Do not compare scores produced with different scopes or tool versions.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports React codebases that can run the React Doctor npm package.

faq.question: Does the skill modify files?
faq.answer: Diagnostic scans report findings. Full triage can edit source files, and rule commands can edit project configuration.

faq.question: Does the skill create commits or pull requests?
faq.answer: No. The documented triage workflow states that it never commits changes or opens pull requests.

faq.question: Does full triage require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It downloads a remote playbook and may fetch remote per-rule guidance.

faq.question: Can it scan only recent changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Changed and changed-line scopes limit diagnostics to recent work.

faq.question: Can I disable a noisy rule?
faq.answer: Yes. First review the explanation, then use the narrowest rule, category, tag, or output-surface control.
